subject: Regional failover automation upgrade — exec update + request to approve prod game day (Jan 15)
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 6, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Regional failover automation upgrade — exec update + request to approve prod game day (Jan 15)

Neha / Irene / Ava — quick exec update on the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade (Reliability Program), plus a request for approval to run our first controlled production failover game day next week.

TL;DR (what’s changing)
- Today failover is a mix of manual actions + partial automation. Triggers have been noisy (false positives), and signal interpretation is inconsistent across Hosted vs Dedicated.
- We’re standardizing a trigger hierarchy (reachability > 5xx burn > tail latency burn > capacity) with dampening/hold-down timers and corroboration requirements.
- We’re adding deterministic evaluation + rollback guardrails (anti-flap, per-tenant safety limits, audit logging).
- We’re validating end-to-end via controlled failover tests (staging first, then limited-blast-radius production).

Why now
- Region-level impairments remain one of the highest customer-visible incident classes for Hosted API (and the most operationally expensive for on-call).
- Our current manual mitigation time + uncertainty causes avoidable error budget burn and can trigger cascading overload when we move traffic late.

Plan (Q1–Q2)
1) Baseline + requirements (now): current-state mapping, incident failure modes, draft SLO targets and trigger hierarchy.
2) Design (in progress): ADRs for signal priority + rollback semantics; runbooks and test plan.
3) Build (Jan): region health aggregator + controller, capacity/network signals, dashboards + burn alerts, incident-bot summaries.
4) Validate (Jan–Feb): staging drills → controlled prod test(s) → tighten based on findings.
5) Rollout + hardening (Feb–Mar): expand coverage by route/model/tier; establish quarterly cadence.

What we need exec approval for
Approval to run Game Day #1: controlled failover of a small slice of Hosted API traffic from us-east → eu-west.
- Proposed window: Thu, Jan 15, 2026, 6:00–7:00 PM PT (off-peak)
- Blast radius: feature-flagged; 1% of traffic for 2 routes; allowlist of ~5 low-risk internal/partner tenants; excludes Dedicated customers.
- Mode: “approval-required automation” (controller computes + proposes; on-call acks before executing).
- Explicit rollback authority: SRE on-call (Rafael/Miles) in coordination with Routing on-call; we revert immediately if guardrail triggers trip.

Success criteria (high-level)
- Failover decision computed within 60–90s of injected impairment signal.
- Customer-visible 5xx stays within planned bounds for the allowlisted tenants (no broad impact).
- No sustained overload in eu-west (capacity gates block if headroom is insufficient).
- Audit trail is complete (who/what/why) and dashboards clearly annotate flips/rollbacks.

Top risks & mitigations
- Trigger noise/false positives: require corroboration + hold-down timers; dry-run mode in prod for 48h before executing.
- DNS / steering uncertainty: we will not change public TTLs for Game Day #1; traffic movement is via routing policy only. Infra changes are staged separately.
- Cascading overload in destination region: capacity signal gates and load shedding / retry-after semantics; automatic stop if eu-west tail latency burn exceeds threshold.
- Operator confusion during event: run-of-show checklist + dedicated observers + comms lead; incident-bot posts automation summary.

Resource asks (for Jan)
- Infra/Network: 1 engineer-week for reachability probe validation + anycast/DNS follow-ups (Victor’s team).
- Control Plane/Routing: 1 engineer-week to finalize deterministic policy evaluation and enable approval hooks.
- Observability: 1 engineer-week to finish dashboard annotations + burn alert tuning.

Attached:
- ExecUpdate_RegionalFailoverAutomationUpgrade_2026-01-06.pdf
- Gameday1_RunOfShow_US-EAST_to_EU-WEST_2026-01-15_v0.3.docx

If you approve, we’ll proceed with the production change request and finalize the go/no-go checklist by EOD Fri (Jan 9).

Please reply with:
1) Approval / conditional approval for the Jan 15 production game day window.
2) Any constraints you want us to bake into go/no-go (e.g., status page notice, customer notifications, additional sign-off).

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, SRE (Reliability Program Lead)
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Jan 6, 2026 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Regional failover automation upgrade — exec update + request to approve prod game day (Jan 15)

Thanks. I’m supportive in principle, but I want a few things explicitly called out before we sign off:

1) Go/no-go criteria: what exact signals/thresholds will block execution that day?
2) Dedicated: confirm no Dedicated tenants are in the allowlist (including “shared” internal accounts that might sit on Dedicated pools).
3) Comms: do we plan a status page notice for a planned test? If not, what’s the escalation plan if there’s unexpected spillover?
4) Data residency: any chance the test inadvertently routes regulated tenants cross-region?

If you can reply with those details + who has rollback authority in real time, I’m comfortable giving approval.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 6, 2026 at 3:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: Regional failover automation upgrade — exec update + request to approve prod game day (Jan 15)

Replying inline.

1) Go/no-go criteria (hard blocks)
We will NOT execute the failover unless all are true at T-15 min:
- Controller is healthy in prod and has been running in dry-run for >= 48 hours with no crashes and stable recommendations.
- Region health service is receiving reachability probe data (no missing-signal gaps) for both us-east and eu-west.
- eu-west capacity gate: >= 30% headroom on the relevant GPU pools for the two target routes, sustained for 30 minutes (no rapid downtrend).
- Error budget burn is nominal prior to start: Hosted multi-region burn alerts are green; no active incident in either region.
- Paging coverage: SRE on-call + Routing on-call + Infra observer in the live channel.

Immediate stop / rollback triggers during execution:
- Allowlisted-tenant 5xx > 1% for > 2 minutes OR any non-allowlisted tenant shows correlated 5xx increase.
- eu-west p99 latency burn crosses the red threshold for 5 minutes.
- Any indication of policy oscillation (anti-flap guardrail trips) or unexpected controller behavior.

2) Dedicated isolation
Confirmed: Dedicated is excluded.
- The allowlist is hosted-only tenants with routing policy scoped by tenant_id + route.
- We will also explicitly denylist known internal accounts that have any Dedicated association (even for test workloads).

3) Comms / status page
For Game Day #1 we’re treating this as an internal reliability exercise with minimal blast radius and no expected customer-visible impact beyond allowlisted tenants.
- Default: no status page notice.
- If we see any impact outside the allowlist (or impact is >5 minutes), we will follow the regional event comms playbook: internal incident declared, status page update drafted by comms lead, Neha (or delegate) approves external updates.
- Ava: we’ll share a short heads-up for Support/CS so they can recognize the window if tickets come in.

4) Data residency
We will only include tenants with no residency constraints.
- The controller enforces policy constraints at evaluation time (tenant tier + residency flag). For this test: any tenant with residency constraints is ineligible for cross-region reroute.

Rollback authority / real-time decisioning
- Execute/rollback: SRE on-call (Rafael) is the operator; Routing on-call is the second set of eyes in the live channel.
- If there’s ambiguity: Rafael will roll back first, then diagnose. No debate while metrics are worsening.

Irene: re: DNS/infra
Correct: no public DNS TTL changes for Game Day #1; the traffic move is via internal routing policy.
If we end up needing any internal infra toggles, they’ll be explicitly listed in the change request (INT-1142) with monitors and a backout plan.

If the above addresses the gating items, please reply “approved” (or “approved w/ conditions”). We’ll lock the go/no-go checklist and schedule a short briefing on Jan 14.

Sean

(Attachment referenced)
- INT-1142 change request will include the final allowlist/denylist and the exact guardrail thresholds for the dashboards/alerts.
